hooks.command: g="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/scripts/fleet_health.py"; [ -f "$g" ] || g="./scripts/fleet_health.py"; [ -f "$g" ] || { echo "[prompts] REFUSED -- the prompts guard could not be LOADED, so this hook refuses what it cannot check. Cause: no scripts/fleet_health.py under CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=[${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR-<unset>}] or cwd=[$PWD]. Fix: start the session from the repo root, or point CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR at it; on a deployed consumer scripts/fleet_health.py ships WITH this hook as ONE floor component -- redeploy the methodology corpus rather than removing the hook." >&2; exit 2; }; out=$(python "$g" --prompts-guard); rc=$?; cr=$(printf '\r'); out=${out%$cr}; [ "$rc" = 2 ] && [ "$out" = "PROMPTS-GUARD-EVALUATED-REFUSE" ] && exit 2; [ "$rc" = 0 ] && [ "$out" = "PROMPTS-GUARD-EVALUATED-OK" ] && exit 0; c="the guard crashed before it could answer -- an import or syntax error in fleet_health.py; its traceback is on stderr above"; [ "$rc" = 127 ] && c="no usable 'python' on PATH -- the interpreter this hook names was not found"; [ "$rc" = 0 ] && c="the interpreter exited 0 but its entire stdout was not exactly the guard's PROMPTS-GUARD-EVALUATED-OK marker, so the guard did NOT run -- the 'python' this hook resolved is a shim, a wrapper, or another interpreter, and an exit of 0 from it is evidence of nothing"; [ "$rc" = 2 ] && c="the interpreter exited 2 WITHOUT the guard's PROMPTS-GUARD-EVALUATED-REFUSE marker, so this is not the guard's verdict -- something exited 2 before reaching it, and a bare refusal with no reason is the failure this hook exists to end"; echo "[prompts] REFUSED -- the prompts guard could not be EVALUATED, so this hook refuses what it cannot check. [$g] exited rc=$rc. Cause: $c. Fix: run 'python scripts/fleet_health.py --prompts-guard' from the repo root; a pass prints PROMPTS-GUARD-EVALUATED-OK and a refusal prints PROMPTS-GUARD-EVALUATED-REFUSE, each as its only stdout. Its stdout here was: [$out]." >&2; exit 2

//: Project-scoped Claude Code hooks for .dev-knowledge. Merges with (does not replace) the user-level ~/.claude/settings.json hooks. uv migration (ADR-106, [#432]): python hook commands run `uv run --locked` so they execute in the declared environment (committed uv.lock); the ONE deliberate exception is the ADR-77 PreToolUse guard below, which stays on the system interpreter — it is stdlib-only and fail-closed, and a stale lockfile must never be able to block every Edit/Write call in a session. PreToolUse: the E-29/013-A prompts-dir scope guard (scripts/fleet_health.py --prompts-guard, matcher narrowed off "*" to the filesystem-touching tool classes by [#684]) -- ARMED 2026-09-07 in the same act as the daemon restart, never before: while the two CLAUDE_PROMPTS_DIR scopes disagree it refuses EVERY tool call with no in-session escape (measured 2026-09-06). Rationale and the two-legged design are in that module's wiring comment. [#684] 2026-09-11 -- the command now RESOLVES ITS OWN ROOT: `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}` prefers the variable and falls back to cwd (hook commands run through a POSIX shell whose cwd is the project dir, measured), and `[ -f "$g" ] || exit 0` made a guard that cannot be LOADED pass instead of refuse -- REVERSED 2026-09-11 by AX15-1, see below. A SECOND `[ -f ]` attempt at cwd was added 2026-09-11 by the fresh Codex review of this branch (HIGH-1): `:-` defaults only on unset-or-empty, so a variable set to the WRONG root skipped the fallback and fell through to fail-open without consulting a guard that was in cwd all along (measured: old rc=0, new rc=7). THE POSTURE INVERTED 2026-09-11 (batch X lane W-2', ruling AX15-1): the command now FAILS CLOSED on every inability to evaluate -- script missing, interpreter missing, crash, any rc other than 0 -- because a guard that permits when it cannot run is declared enforcement without enforcement. Only rc=0 whose ENTIRE stdout is the guard's own PROMPTS-GUARD-EVALUATED-OK marker passes -- one trailing CR tolerated, stripped with shell builtins so an emptied PATH cannot break it, because a Python build that emits CRLF must never be able to refuse every tool call. Containment was the first form and round 2 of the same review broke it: stdout reading 'not-PROMPTS-GUARD-EVALUATED-OK-proof' satisfied it. The accidental shims never emit the token at all, so this closes the deliberate case, and it closes it for free: the 2026-09-11 fresh Codex review (HIGH-1) found the last inferred permit here -- an exit of 0 on its own is byte-identical to what a shim, a wrapper or the wrong 'python' first on PATH produces, so the hook was reading the ABSENCE of an error as proof of a check it never got. The permit is now proven, not assumed. ROUND 3 closed the mirror hole on the other verdict: rc=2 went straight to a bare exit 2, so a python shim exiting 2 -- or this file dying of SystemExit(2) above prompts_guard() -- refused the seat with an EMPTY stderr, which is MA-1's presentation exactly and was the last route by which this hook could stop a session without saying why. A refusal now must carry PROMPTS-GUARD-EVALUATED-REFUSE, a deliberately DIFFERENT token, and anything else exiting 2 gets the teaching message instead. What the impostor printed is quoted back in that message, so the reader sees the evidence rather than a verdict. NOT CLOSED, and not closable here: a shim that prints the exact marker and exits 0 still permits. The hook's only channel to the guard is an interpreter the PATH chooses, so any token the guard can emit a substitute can emit too -- there is no secret to share with a prover the attacker selects. It is also moot: whoever controls that python controls the guard's answer outright. What exists instead is DETECTION -- the SessionStart preflight prints the absolute path of the interpreter it resolved through the hook's own PATH, so a shadowed python is visible at boot. fleet_health.py's GUARD_EVALUATED_MARKER is the one home for that token and a wiring test reads it from there to assert this command still tests for it, so the two halves cannot drift apart silently. Each refusal names its CAUSE and its FIX on stderr, which is what makes this different from the MA-1 failure it superficially resembles: MA-1 refused SILENTLY and presented as the reader being broken. Two things pay for the inversion and neither may be removed without re-opening it: the MATCHER stays narrowed (the break-glass family is ungated, so a refusing guard still leaves an in-session way out), and scripts/fleet_health.py's SessionStart leg preflights interpreter + guard script once at boot, so a per-call refusal is the exception rather than the first news. AX15-2 couples the two halves: this hook block and scripts/fleet_health.py are ONE floor component, and a repo carrying the hook without the script is a fleet_parity MUST-absent (surface settings-prompts-guard-coupling), never a silent permit. CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is set by Claude Code and by nothing else, so the old bare form turned any other reader honouring this file (cursor-agent, measured over two paid runs) into total refusal of every tool call, presenting as the reader being broken. Nothing the guard guards is weakened -- where the script resolves it runs with full force and a mismatch still exits 2. See docs/audits/2026-09-10-technical-night-aj-m03/REVIEW.md:83 and tests/test_prompts_guard_hook_wiring.py. The MATCHER also narrowed in the same act, off "*" to Read|Write|Edit|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Glob|Grep|Bash|PowerShell|Monitor|LSP|ReadMcpResourceTool|mcp__.* -- the classes a stale CLAUDE_PROMPTS_DIR actually makes lie. The MCP and secondary filesystem routes (Monitor, LSP, ReadMcpResourceTool, mcp__.*) were added 2026-09-11 by the fresh Codex review of this branch (HIGH-2), which is right that an MCP filesystem tool could reach a stale scope without passing the guard. Its other two names are REFUSED on the merits: EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree are the break-glass family, and gating the DESTINATION of the ToolSearch escape route defeats the route as surely as gating the route itself. The refusal is NOT narrowed: a mismatch still stops the seat at its first file-touching call, which is the first thing any session does. What the narrowing buys is the break-glass: matcher "*" gated ToolSearch too, and ToolSearch is the only route to the deferred ExitWorktree / SendMessage tools, so the 2026-09-06 wedge could not be undone from inside the session at all (recovery took an external shell). Then the ADR-77 immutability guard (scripts/hooks/block_immutable_edits.py) blocks in-place edits of existing transcripts under docs/decisions/transcripts/** (fail-closed in-zone, fail-open out-of-zone; follows the global block-onedrive template) — refs #105. SessionStart: Tier-2 fleet-health + triage surfacing + billing-leak sentinel + changelog version sentinel (#113 — LOCAL, fail-soft: nudges /changelog-review when an installed tool version exceeds its last_reviewed in ecosystem/tool-versions.yaml; no network) + RF-2 hub self-arm (`scripts/arm_hooks.py` — idempotent, fail-soft `pre-commit install` of the 3 hook types; makes the hub apply configured->armed->proven to ITSELF, closing the configured-not-armed window a fresh clone or a deleted hook opens; quiet no-op when already armed; core.hooksPath-tolerant; Fable architecture review 2026-07-04 §4; asserted by audit.py check_hooks_armed). Tier-1 closure loop runs via the enabled tier1-lifecycle plugin (Stop->propose) + the global ~/.claude surface hook (#73 5c convergence).
//autoMode: A2 hardening on the #86 cloud-night envelope (Arc 5, architect-ruled land-now 2026-07-06; source: docs/audits/2026-07-06-changelog-review.md A2). Native auto-mode safety nets: 2.1.178 pre-launch subagent classification + 2.1.183 destructive-git blocks are automatic in auto mode; classifyAllShell (2.1.193) additionally routes ALL Bash/PowerShell through the classifier, not just arbitrary-code-exec patterns. RECONCILIATION vs the deny-first floor (reconcile-or-reject, ruled): RECONCILED as a layered ADDITIVE net — the deny-first floor (PreToolUse guards, platform guards, deny-beats-allow) stays authoritative and is not weakened; these nets fire only in auto-mode contexts (the unattended nightly), can only BLOCK more (never grant), and are inert in the operator's interactive modes. Reinforces core-invariant #3; replaces nothing.
//permissions: Cloud-night safety envelope (platform-guards model; advances #86). Pre-allows the Workflow tool. A2 layer (2026-07-06): see //autoMode — native auto-mode nets harden the unattended path as a complementary layer. RUNTIME REALITY (re-probed 2026-06-04): the native Workflow launcher is NOT enabled in the cloud context (Claude Code on the web / Routines), so the canonical cloud execution path is SPEC-ORCHESTRATION -- the nightly Routine reads .claude/workflows/conformance-hub.js as the canonical SPECIFICATION and executes its three stages via read-only Explore agents (the script's exact stage prompts + schemas; Sonnet verifiers, Opus skeptic/digest). Each nightly run ATTEMPTS the native launcher first and falls back to spec-orchestration -- a free nightly re-probe; the digest reports which path ran, and execution swaps back to native automatically when the platform re-enables it. The Workflow allow is retained for local sessions (where the launcher works) and for that cloud re-enable. NO Write/Edit deny is committed by design: deny beats allow with no path carve-outs, so a blanket deny would break BOTH local daily work and the routine's own digest write. Cloud subagent containment is instead provided by platform guards -- Routines push only to claude/* branches, every run lands in a PR (no auto-merge), the conformance review is read-only by design (schema-bound agents that never write), and the Routine prompt runs a post-run `git status --porcelain` tripwire reported in the PR/digest.
//worktree: [#716] A lane branches from the DISPATCHING checkout's HEAD, not from origin/main. Unset means 'fresh', which binds the base to a REMOTE ref the dispatcher does not control: with anything unpushed on local main, every lane starts behind, and a generator run against a lagging base silently DROPS rows that exist on main -- the dropped row looks like a clean regeneration. Measured on lane-x-716 itself: the lane sent to fix this branched SEVEN commits behind. The operator dispatches from the primary checkout ('from the target repo root'), which sits on main, so 'head' resolves to main HEAD. It is not a guarantee on its own -- a dispatcher on a feature branch would seed lanes from THAT branch -- which is why the PROPERTY is asserted by a test rather than by this value: scripts/worktree_seed.py::base_ref_verdict, witnessed by tests/test_worktree_seed.py::test_A_LANES_BASE_EQUALS_MAIN_HEAD_AT_DISPATCH. Key shape verified against the shipped Claude Code 2.1.268 binary: NESTED under 'worktree', enum exactly {fresh|head}; a flat 'worktree.baseRef' key is ignored in silence.
